lesson: New Keys up to Four Sharps or Flats

findings.issue: The ABC pitches are an octave higher than the same triad shown on the keyboard and play blocks. In ABC, [Ace] under K:Ab decodes to A flat4, C5, E flat5, but block 136 (keyboard) and blocks 137/138 (play) all use A flat3, C4, E flat4. The parallel F minor set (142/144/145) is internally consistent, so this octave mismatch is a real inconsistency.
findings.evidence: abc "[Ace]4" = Ab4/C5/Eb5 vs keyboard highlight "Ab3","C4","Eb4" and play notes "Ab3","C4","Eb4"
findings.fix: Write the ABC as [A,CE] so the staff shows A flat3, C4, E flat4, matching the keyboard and audio.

findings.issue: The callout repeats the enharmonic point (B sharp = C) already stated in the immediately preceding text block 46, so the two consecutive blocks say the same thing.
findings.evidence: Block 46: "B sharp is the same key as C." Block 47: "B sharp and C natural are the same key (enharmonic)"
findings.fix: Merge into one statement; keep the enharmonic recap in the callout and drop the duplicate sentence from block 46 (or vice versa).
